activities.name: Arrive and drop bags
activities.description: Land, train into Santa Apolónia, and hand bags to the guesthouse before rooms open.

dining.name: Pastelaria Santo António
dining.description: Two minutes from the guesthouse door — a bica and a warm pastel de nata is all a jet-lagged first morning needs before the hills.

activities.name: Alfama backstreet wander
activities.description: No map for two hours between the cathedral and the river: you asked for unplanned time, and Alfama's laundry-strung lanes reward it better than any list.

activities.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
activities.description: Arrive near five when the tour groups thin and the azulejo terrace catches low light over the rooftops you just walked.

dining.name: Ti-Natércia
dining.description: Eight tables halfway up your afternoon route; Natércia's chouriço assado and house wine suit the slow first day you planned.

activities.name: Fado at Tasca do Chico
activities.description: You ranked live music first, so it opens the trip: amateur fado a five-minute walk downhill, raw in the way the tourist dinner-shows are not.

dining.name: Taberna Sal Grosso
dining.description: Around the corner from the fado house — split small plates late, the way the neighborhood actually eats after a show.

activities.name: Castelo de São Jorge early
activities.description: Book the 9am slot: you share the ramparts with peacocks instead of cruise crowds, and the climb starts from yesterday's streets — no transit needed.

activities.name: Graça viewpoint coffee
activities.description: Fifteen minutes further uphill, the miradouro kiosk where castle visitors rarely continue; the view back covers everything you walked yesterday.

dining.name: O Vinhaça
dining.description: On the walk between castle and Graça — grilled sardines at the counter, priced for the builders who eat here daily.

activities.name: Feira da Ladra market
activities.description: Tuesday is market day, which is why this sits on day 2: tiles, brass, and junk spread over the Graça hillside you are already on.

dining.name: Cantina Baldracca
dining.description: Italian-Portuguese counter beside the market field; the daily pasta is what the stallholders themselves queue for at two.

activities.name: Open evening in Graça
activities.description: Yesterday ran late, so tonight stays loose: the kiosk terraces around Graça square fill with neighbors at dusk and need no plan.

dining.name: Damas
dining.description: A Graça bakery by day and bar by night — dinner where the evening already is, no cab across town.

activities.name: Tram 15 to Jerónimos
activities.description: The 8:40 tram beats both the traffic and the monastery queue; being inside by 9:30 buys you the cloisters nearly alone.

activities.name: Jerónimos Monastery cloisters
activities.description: The Manueline carving you flagged in your saved photos is here — an hour in the cloisters, skipping the church line entirely.

dining.name: Pastéis de Belém
dining.description: The original bakery is 200 meters from the monastery exit; eat the custard tarts warm at the azulejo counter, not from the takeaway line.

activities.name: MAAT and riverside walk
activities.description: The riverfront path links the monastery to MAAT in twenty flat minutes, so the museum, the bridge views, and the walk are one continuous afternoon.

dining.name: Este Oeste
dining.description: On the riverside path itself between MAAT and the tower — wood-fired pizza on the terrace saves you leaving the waterfront.

activities.name: Sunset at Belém Tower
activities.description: Stay riverside for the light: the tower faces west, and the lawns fill with locals with bottles of vinho verde around eight.

dining.name: A Margem
dining.description: A glass cube on the water fifty meters from the tower — book the 8:30 table so dinner starts as the sky goes pink.

activities.name: Slow Baixa breakfast
activities.description: A deliberately empty last morning: Rua Augusta before the shops open, when the mosaics are wet from washing and the arch frames an empty street.

dining.name: Confeitaria Nacional
dining.description: Lisbon's oldest pastry house sits on your walk through Praça da Figueira — a last bica under the same mirrors since 1829.

activities.name: Last souvenirs on Rua da Conceição
activities.description: The haberdashery block of Baixa, where the tinned-fish and tile shops are actual old suppliers rather than airport-brand outlets.

activities.name: Airport transfer
activities.description: Metro from Baixa-Chiado runs direct to the airport in 25 minutes — leave three hours before the flight.

dining.name: Nicolau Lisboa
dining.description: Brunch plates two streets from the metro entrance; a proper sit-down lunch beats airport food and still makes the 2pm train.

activities.name: Departure
activities.description: Flight home; the evening belongs to the airline.
